items.title: Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: So, next band I got with was Kid Renee. Well, I stayed with Kid Renee a good while. And I was- That was the brass band or the dance band? No, dance band.

ctx.x: With Pete there. So we'd go to the barbershop on Bienville Street there and we'd rehearsal up near him and I just the bass and the trombone. So this fella, Amos White. That's right. Amos White would come along and he'd join in with us and he would write off a little piece of music there and make me go over that music, you know, and so finally I got pretty good with it. And so this little band formed up as I went with them. They call it the Bulls Band. So I went on and started playing with them. So first job they…
I was going to ask some more about some of the names you mentioned, uh, Eddie Jackson on tuba. Eddie Jackson on tuba. People tell me he was pretty good. Was he really that good?

items.title: Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: brought him on up to the hotel there he was staying at that hotel on Julia and Ramport

ctx.x: bands down there to meet them or something they had uh they had one brass band and if I'm not mistaken they had one band in in a wagon like you know playing on a playing on the furniture wagon yeah
I thought maybe Kid René or somebody was there at that time yeah in a wagon you were with him

I don't remember what band it was that was in the wagon but I know we was the marching band you see and uh because we played we played on true canal street and brought him on up to the hotel there he was staying at that hotel on Julia and Ramport what do you call it the Patterson? Patterson Hotel yeah
